alternatives.root_cause: frontend was cut off from the network and could not reach product-catalog.
alternatives.why_not: A partitioned but running service keeps logging its failures to reach peers; frontend wrote nothing at all after ~03:01 (tr_ae25c99037cd), and it had earlier logged connection errors normally, showing it logs when it can run.

alternatives.root_cause: product-catalog became slow and frontend failed because it waited.
alternatives.why_not: product-catalog served other callers with sub-10ms spans throughout and showed no error-ratio departure (tr_173364a2eeae, tr_8b3eba96b0e1); the frontend's stalled gRPC spans have no matching server span, so the time was never spent inside product-catalog.

alternatives.root_cause: A bad artifact or configuration was rolled out to frontend.
alternatives.why_not: The change log for frontend over the preceding 24 hours was observed and empty (tr_accc0d287580), and the service served normal traffic minutes before the stall.

verdict.summary: The frontend process stopped executing while its socket kept accepting connections, so proxy requests hung to their 15s deadlines and in-flight gRPC calls to product-catalog sat for minutes without ever reaching it.
verdict.reasoning: frontend-proxy and load-generator alerted, but their traces (tr_748cf57731a4) show every failing request terminating at the proxy's fixed ~15s deadline while the frontend spans beneath continue for 250-300s, with the frontend's own gRPC client spans holding nearly all of that time as self-time and producing no child span at the callee. The suspected callee, product-catalog, is demonstrably healthy over the same window: it keeps serving recommendation's ListProducts calls (tr_173364a2eeae, tr_dfb1a3e72ee0) and its error ratio does not depart from baseline (tr_8b3eba96b0e1), with its only log noise being telemetry export deadlines (tr_6125406c5dd7). So the stall is on the frontend side of that hop, not in the dependency. frontend's error ratio never rises (tr_c9b7254728c4) - requests are not failing, they are not completing - and its log goes silent well before the stated onset and stays silent (tr_ae25c99037cd), which is the signature of a stopped process rather than a partitioned one, which would log its inability to reach peers. No deploy or config change exists for frontend or product-catalog in the preceding day (tr_accc0d287580, tr_060a332d7f69), ruling out artifact and configuration causes.
open_questions: Whether the freeze was continuous from ~03:01 to the end of the window or intermittent, since the log result elided the middle and only the oldest and newest lines were returned.
What stopped the process - a SIGSTOP, a full GC/event-loop stall, or node-level pressure - which would distinguish a true freeze from resource exhaustion inside the runtime.
frontend-proxy produced no log lines at all (tr_590dd39896e4), so the proxy's own view of the upstream (timeout vs reset) was not confirmed independently of traces.
Why the declared onset is 03:17:46 when hanging traces appear from ~02:56 onward.
